_comment: Stem counts read off real scanned cells by eye (Sean, 2026-08-28). Before
this there was no stem ground truth on a real score at all, which blocked
judging both the residual over-count on the LilyPond reference sheet and
the ~30% of stems that a raised height floor would have removed.
Counting rule given: one stem per note OR CHORD — three noteheads sharing
one stem count once. Whole notes have none. Barlines, ledger lines and the
vertical strokes of sharps, naturals and flats are NOT stems; that last
exclusion is the whole point of the exercise.
The cells were chosen adversarially rather than at random: eleven are cells
where the two candidate settings (a 2.0- and a 2.8-staff-space height
floor) disagreed, by up to 10 stems, so a hand count decides between them
directly. Four are controls where the two settings agree.
WHAT IT DECIDED. Neither height floor is right, and the failure is
asymmetric by score. The 2.8 floor is nearly exact on Boléro (|err| 1 over
4 cells) because there the surplus really was accidental strokes — but it
destroys keyboard music, where stems in beamed groups are legitimately
short: one WTC cell holds 15 stems and the 2.8 floor finds 5. Height is the
wrong discriminator. What separates them is that an accidental's strokes
come in PAIRS and a stem is single; that rule takes summed |error| from 60
to 24 here, and the reference sheet from +7 to -1 on a truth of 48.
